verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：天是我的座位；地是我的脚凳。你们要为我造何等的殿宇？哪里是我安息的地方呢？
verses.en: This is what the Lord says:“The heavens are my throneand the earth is my footstool.Where then is the house you will build for me?Where is the place where I will rest?
verses.commentary:
66:1 "Heaven is My throne and the earth is My footstool.

Where then is a house you could build for Me?

And where is a place that I may rest?"

This is an obvious allusion to the dedicatory prayer of Solomon in 1 Kgs. 8:27 and is again
alluded to in Acts 7:47-50.

What is difficult to know is to what historical period this relates. Some see it relating to the return
from the exile and the rebuilding of the temple, which is possible from the larger context. However, others say that God
does not live in manmade buildings and that this refers to

- the temple of the human body which God has made

- the family of God, the faith seed of Abraham (Jews and Gentiles of faith, cf. Rom. 2:28-29)

- the cosmic temple of Genesis 1 where Elohim may "rest" (cf. Gen. 2:2),
see John H. Walton, The Lost World of Genesis One: An Ancient Cosmology

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE HEAVENS AND THE THIRD HEAVEN

▣ "My footstool" (BDB 919) This imagery has three orientations.

- earth is YHWH's footstool (i.e. He is the Creator and King, cf. Isa. 66:1)

- the Ark of the Covenant is YHWH's footstool (the temple is where His presence resides, cf. 1 Chr. 28:2;
Ps. 99:5; 132:7; Lam. 2:1)

SPECIAL TOPIC: THE ARK OF THE COVENANT

- YHWH's enemies and the enemies of His people will be His footstool (i.e. imagery of victory, cf. Ps. 110:1; Matt. 22:44;
Mark 12:36; Luke 20:43; Acts 2:35; Heb. 1:13; 10:13

verses.zh: 耶和华说：这一切都是我手所造的，所以就都有了。但我所看顾的，就是虚心（原文是贫穷）痛悔、因我话而战兢的人。
verses.en: My hand made them;[NOTE:1] that is how they came to be,”[NOTE:2] says the Lord.“I show special favor[NOTE:3] to the humble and contrite,who respect what I have to say.[NOTE:4]
notes: Heb “all these.” The phrase refers to the heavens and earth, mentioned in the previous verse.
Heb “and all these were.” Some prefer to emend וַיִּהְיוּ (vayyihyu, “and they were”) to וְלִי הָיוּ (veli hayu, “and to me they were”), i.e., “and they belong to me.”
Heb “and to this one I look” (KJV and NASB both similar).
Heb “to the humble and the lowly in spirit and the one who trembles at my words.”
verses.commentary:
66:2 "For My hand made all these things" We learn from the NT that God's agent in creation was no one
other than the pre-Incarnate Jesus Christ (cf. John 1:3; 1 Cor. 8:6; Col. 1:16; Heb. 1:2).

SPECIAL TOPIC: HAND

▣

NASB, JPSOA
"came into being"

NKJV
"exist"

NRSV, LXX
"are mine"

REB, Peshitta
"belong to me"

The MT has the "to be" VERB (BDB 224, KB 243, Qal PERFECT
with waw). The UBS Text Project, p. 168, gives this a "B" rating (some doubt).

The ancient versions understood it as affirming YHWH's ownership because He was their creator.

▣ "But to this one I will look,

To him who is humble and contrite of spirit,

and who trembles at My word"

God looks first
at the motives and character of the human heart. YHWH knows the thoughts and intents of the heart (cf. 1 Sam. 2:3; 16:7;
1 Kgs. 8:39; 1 Chr. 28:9; 2 Chr. 6:30; Ps. 7:9; 17:3; 26:2; 44:21; 139:1,23; Prov. 15:11; 16:2; 21:2; 24:12; Jer. 11:20; 17:9-10; 20:12;
Luke 16:15; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27). Jesus also knows the inner thoughts and motives of humans, see John 2:24-25; 6:61,64; 13:11!

This same description is used of David's contrition over the sin with Bathsheba (cf. Ps. 51:17);
note Isa. 57:15; Ps. 34:18; Matt. 5:3-4; Luke 18:13-14.

This also has two descriptions of God's true people that are very beautiful and descriptive.

- a humble people (BDB 776)

- contrite people (BDB 646, cf. Isa. 57:15)

- those who tremble at His word (BDB 353, cf. Isa. 66:5)

▣ "of spirit" See SPECIAL TOPIC: SPIRIT IN THE BIBLE.

verses.zh: 假冒为善的宰牛，好像杀人，献羊羔，好像打折狗项，献供物，好像献猪血，烧乳香，好像称颂偶像。这等人拣选自己的道路，心里喜悦行可憎恶的事。
verses.en: The one who slaughters a bull also strikes down a man;[NOTE:1] the one who sacrifices a lamb also breaks a dog’s neck;[NOTE:2] the one who presents an offering includes pig’s blood with it;[NOTE:3] the one who offers incense also praises an idol.[NOTE:4] They have decided to behave this way;[NOTE:5] they enjoy these disgusting practices.[NOTE:6]
notes: Heb “one who slaughters a bull, one who strikes down a man.” Some understand a comparison here and in the following lines. In God’s sight the one who sacrifices is like (i.e., regarded as) a murderer or one whose worship is ritually defiled or idolatrous. The translation above assumes that the language is not metaphorical, but descriptive of the sinners’ hypocritical behavior. (Note the last two lines of the verse, which suggest they are guilty of abominable practices.) On the one hand, they act pious and offer sacrifices, but at the same time they commit violent crimes against men, defile their sacrifices, and worship other gods.

Heb “one who sacrifices a lamb, one who breaks a dog’s neck.” Some understand a comparison, but see the previous note.sn The significance of breaking a dog’s neck is uncertain, though the structure of the statement when compared to the preceding and following lines suggests the action is viewed in a negative light. According to Exod 13:13 and 34:20, one was to “redeem” a firstborn donkey by offering a lamb; if one did not “redeem” the firstborn donkey in this way, then its neck must be broken. According to Deut 21:1-9 a heifer’s neck was to be broken as part of the atonement ritual to purify the land from the guilt of bloodshed. It is not certain if these passages relate in any way to the action described in Isa 66:3.
Heb “one who offers an offering, pig’s blood.” Some understand a comparison, but see the note at the end of the first line.

Heb “one who offers incense as a memorial offering, one who blesses something false.” Some understand a comparison, but see the note at the end of the first line. אָוֶן (ʾaven), which has a wide variety of attested nuances, here refers metonymically to an idol. See HALOT 22 s.v. and BDB 20 s.v. 2.
Heb “also they have chosen their ways.”
Heb “their being [or “soul”] takes delight in their disgusting [things].”
verses.commentary:
66:3-4 This shows that ritual alone is not satisfactory (cf. Isa. 29:13; Jeremiah 7), but combined
with ritual must be a humble and repentant heart. That which we do over and over again tends to become
common, but in the area of faith, our motive is the key (cf. Isa. 66:2).

66:3 "And their soul delights in their abominations" This refers to various pagan worship rites
(cf. Isa. 65:4,7,11; see SPECIAL TOPIC: MAGIC and SPECIAL TOPIC: IDOLATRY).
They loved and chose (BDB 103, KB 119, used three times in Isa. 66:3-4) sin (cf. Isa. 1:4; 57:17; 65:2; 66:18; Ps. 81:11-12)!

For "soul" see SPECIAL TOPIC: NEPHESH

For "abominations" see SPECIAL TOPIC: ABOMINATION (OT)

verses.zh: 我也必拣选迷惑他们的事，使他们所惧怕的临到他们；因为我呼唤，无人答应；我说话，他们不听从；反倒行我眼中看为恶的，拣选我所不喜悦的。
verses.en: So I will choose severe punishment[NOTE:1] for them;I will bring on them what they dreadbecause I called, and no one responded.I spoke and they did not listen.They did evil before me;[NOTE:2] they chose to do what displeases me.”
notes: The precise meaning of the noun is uncertain. It occurs only here and in 3:4 (but see the note there). It appears to be derived from the verbal root עָלַל (ʿalal), which can carry the nuance “deal severely.”
Heb “that which is evil in my eyes.”
verses.commentary:
66:4

NASB
"punishments"

NKJV
"delusions"

NRSV, JPSOA
"mock"

TEV
"disaster"

NJB
"making fools of them"

REB
"a willful course"

Peshitta
"humiliated"

The word (BDB 760, KB 1768) is found only here and Isa. 3:4.

- BDB suggests "wanton dealings"

- KB suggests

- acts of mischief (done by a child from the root, עולל (BDB 760) for Isa. 3:4

- ill treatment, here

- The NET Bible, p. 2286, #6, gets a meaning from עלל (BDB 760), "deal severely."

▣ "And will bring on them what they dread" Oh my! What a terrible curse from God (cf. Prov. 1:27; 10:24)!

▣ "Because I called, but no one answered" Here again is the repetition of the theme of no faith, no repentant
response from YHWH's covenant people (cf. Isa. 41:28; 50:2; 65:12).

verses.zh: 你们因耶和华言语战兢的人当听他的话：你们的弟兄―就是恨恶你们，因我名赶出你们的，曾说：愿耶和华得荣耀，使我们得见你们的喜乐；但蒙羞的究竟是他们！
verses.en: Listen to the Lord’s message,you who respect[NOTE:1] his word! “Your countrymen,[NOTE:2] who hate you and exclude you, supposedly for the sake of my name,say, ‘May the Lord be glorified,then we will witness your joy.’[NOTE:3] But they will be put to shame.
notes: Heb “tremble.”
Heb “brothers” (so NASB, NIV84); NIV11, NRSV “Your own people”; NLT “Your close relatives.”
Or “so that we might witness your joy.” The point of this statement is unclear.
verses.commentary:
66:5 There is a distress and tension within the people of God (cf. Rom. 9:6-8). The persecution
of the prophets by fellow Judeans is a good example of this (cf. Matt. 5:10-12; 10:22). Many horrible things have been
done by "religious" people in God's name!

Notice how the true people of God should respond to persecution ‒ joy (BDB 970,
cf. Isa. 51:11; 55:12; 61:7; note 66:10 which has several other words synonymous with joy. Jesus talks about God's joy often in
John's Gospel (cf. John 3:29; 15:11; 16:24; 17:13).

- be glad ‒ BDB 162

- rejoice ‒ BDB 965 (twice)

- also Qal IMPERATIVE of "joy" (BDB 970)

There are three commands in Isa. 66:5.

- Hear the word of the Lord ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 1033, KB 1570

- Let the Lord be glorified ‒ Qal IMPERFECT,
BDB 457, KB 455, used in a JUSSIVE sense (the LXX translates it as PASSIVE)

- That we may see your joy ‒ Qal IMPERFECT, BDB 906, KB 157, used in a
COHORTATIVE sense

verses.zh: 有喧哗的声音出自城中！有声音出于殿中！是耶和华向仇敌施行报应的声音！
verses.en: The sound of battle comes from the city;the sound comes from the temple!It is the sound of the Lord paying back his enemies.
verses.commentary:
66:6 There has been much discussion among commentators about how this verse relates to the
context. Some say it is an unknown historical event, while others say it is related directly to Isa. 66:5, which
shows the judgment of prideful, unbelieving Judeans (i.e. here called "enemies").

verses.zh: 锡安未曾劬劳就生产，未觉疼痛就生出男孩。
verses.en: Before she goes into labor, she gives birth!Before her contractions begin, she delivers a boy!
verses.commentary:
66:7-13 This context refers to Zion bringing forth a nation in one day which includes Gentiles. Some
see this as the return from exile, but in this event no Gentiles were included. Therefore, it must be eschatological (i.e. NT).

verses.zh: 国岂能一日而生？民岂能一时而产？因为锡安一劬劳便生下儿女，这样的事谁曾听见？谁曾看见呢？
verses.en: Who has ever heard of such a thing?Who has ever seen this?Can a country[NOTE:1] be brought forth in one day?Can a nation be born in a single moment?Yet as soon as Zion goes into labor she gives birth to sons!
notes: Heb “land,” but here אֶרֶץ (ʾerets) stands metonymically for an organized nation (see the following line).

verses.zh: 耶和华说：我既使她临产，岂不使她生产呢？你的　神说：我既使她生产，岂能使她闭胎不生呢？
verses.en: Do I bring a baby to the birth opening and then not deliver it?”asks the Lord.“Or do I bring a baby to the point of delivery and then hold it back?”asks your God.[NOTE:1]
notes: The rhetorical questions expect the answer, “Of course not!”

verses.zh: 你们爱慕耶路撒冷的都要与她一同欢喜快乐；你们为她悲哀的都要与她一同乐上加乐；
verses.en: “Be happy for Jerusalemand rejoice with her, all you who love her!Share in her great joy,all you who have mourned over her!
verses.commentary:
66:10 As a result of what YHWH has done in restoring His people to their Promised Land
(i.e. Gen. 12:1; 15:16), the commands are

- be joyful ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 970, KB 1333

- rejoice ‒ Qal IMPERATIVE, BDB 162, KB 189

- be exceedingly glad ‒ the Qal IMPERATIVE and the NOUN, BDB 965, KB 965

verses.zh: 使你们在她安慰的怀中吃奶得饱，使他们得她丰盛的荣耀，犹如挤奶，满心喜乐。
verses.en: For[NOTE:1] you will nurse from her satisfying breasts and be nourished;[NOTE:2] you will feed with joy from her milk-filled breasts.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Or “in order that”; ASV, NRSV “that.”
Heb “you will suck and be satisfied from her comforting breast.”
Zion’s residents will benefit from and enjoy her great material prosperity. See v. 12. tn Heb “you will slurp and refresh yourselves from her heavy breast.”
verses.commentary:
66:11-12 Nursing imagery is used of YHWH's mercy. Please listen to my audio sermon, "The Femininity of God"
(second green box on my homepage, www.freebiblecommentary.org, #111).

verses.zh: 耶和华如此说：我要使平安延及她，好像江河，使列国的荣耀延及她，如同涨溢的河。你们要从中享受（原文是咂）；你们必蒙抱在肋旁，摇弄在膝上。
verses.en: For this is what the Lord says:“Look, I am ready to extend to her prosperity that will flow like a river,the riches of nations will flow into her like a stream that floods its banks.[NOTE:1] You will nurse from her breast[NOTE:2] and be carried at her side;you will play on her knees.
notes: Heb “Look, I am ready to extend to her like a river prosperity [or “peace”], and like an overflowing stream, the riches of nations.”
The words “from her breast” are supplied in the translation for clarification (see v. 11).
verses.commentary:
66:12 The parental imagery of God's love for His people is so powerful in this verse. YHWH is
described in feminine imagery (cf. Isa. 49:15; 66:9-13).

The fact that God would use "a nursing woman" to describe Himself says volumes.

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN THE BIBLE

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN IN MINISTRY

SPECIAL TOPIC: WOMEN MINISTERS

verses.zh: 母亲怎样安慰儿子，我就照样安慰你们；你们也必因（或译：在）耶路撒冷得安慰。
verses.en: As a mother consoles a child,[NOTE:1] so I will console you,and you will be consoled over Jerusalem.”
notes: Heb “like a man whose mother comforts him.”
verses.commentary:
66:13 The word "comforts" (BDB 636, KB 688) is used three times in this verse.

- Piel IMPERFECT (twice)

- same as #1

- Pual IMPERFECT

This reminds one of Isa. 40:1 (Piel IMPERATIVE, twice); also note Isa. 12:1;
53:3 (twice),12,19; 52:9; 61:2 (57:18, BDB 637). This is a major theme of Isaiah 40-66. YHWH has acted to forgive,
forget, and restore those who trust Him and tremble at His word (Isa. 66:2,5)!

SPECIAL TOPIC: COMFORT

verses.zh: 你们看见，就心中快乐；你们的骨头必得滋润像嫩草一样；而且耶和华的手向他仆人所行的必被人知道；他也要向仇敌发恼恨。
verses.en: When you see this, you will be happy,[NOTE:1] and you will be revived.[NOTE:2] The Lord will reveal his power to his servantsand his anger to his enemies.[NOTE:3]
notes: “and you will see and your heart will be happy.”
Heb “and your bones like grass will sprout.”
Heb “and the hand of the Lord will be made known to his servants, and anger to his enemies.”

verses.zh: 看哪，耶和华必在火中降临；他的车辇像旋风，以烈怒施行报应，以火焰施行责罚；
verses.en: For look, the Lord comes with fire;his chariots come like a windstorm[NOTE:1] to reveal his raging anger,his battle cry, and his flaming arrows.[NOTE:2]
notes: Chariots are like a windstorm in their swift movement and in the way that they kick up dust.
Heb “to cause to return with the rage of his anger, and his battle cry [or “rebuke”] with flames of fire.”
verses.commentary:
66:15-16 Notice the different images used to describe YHWH's judgment.

- fire (BDB 77; see SPECIAL TOPIC: FIRE)

- whirlwind (BDB 693 I, cf. Isa. 5:28; Jer. 4:13)

- His anger (BDB 60 I) with fury (BDB 404, cf. Isa. 42:25; 51:20; 63:3,6)

- His rebuke with flames of fire, cf. Isa. 29:6; 30:30

- judgment by fire

- His sword on all flesh, cf. Isa. 65:12

verses.zh: 因为耶和华在一切有血气的人身上，必以火与刀施行审判；被耶和华所杀的必多。
verses.en: For the Lord judges all humanity[NOTE:1] with fire and his sword;the Lord will kill many.[NOTE:2]
notes: Heb “flesh” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV); NIV84 “all men”; NIV11 “all people”; TEV “all the people of the world.”
Heb “many are the slain of the Lord.”
verses.commentary:
66:16 "those slain by the Lord will be many" This shows that judgment
will begin with the household of God. We need to remember that there are many within the covenant community
and, God help us, within the Church, who do not really know the Messiah.

SPECIAL TOPIC: KNOW

verses.zh: 「那些分别为圣、洁净自己的，进入园内跟在其中一个人的后头，吃猪肉和仓鼠并可憎之物，他们必一同灭绝；这是耶和华说的。
verses.en: “As for those who consecrate and ritually purify themselves so they can follow their leader and worship in the sacred orchards,[NOTE:1] those who eat the flesh of pigs and other disgusting creatures, like mice[NOTE:2]—they will all be destroyed together,”[NOTE:3] says the Lord.
notes: Heb “the ones who consecrate themselves and the ones who purify themselves toward the orchards [or “gardens”] after the one in the midst.” The precise meaning of the statement is unclear, though it is obvious that some form of idolatry is in view.
Heb “ones who eat the flesh of the pig and the disgusting thing and the mouse.”
Heb “together they will come to an end.”
verses.commentary:
66:17 "to the gardens" This is a reference to a place of pagan worship (cf. Isa. 65:3).

▣ "Following one in the center" The word translated "center" (BDB 1063) is also used of
the "tree of life" in Gen. 3:3. The Septuagint sees Isa. 65:22 as also referring to the tree of life. Here this may
refer to the Asherah poles or carved stake of Canaanite fertility worship.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FERTILITY WORSHIP OF THE ANE

▣ "Who eat. . ."

- swine's flesh, cf. Isa. 65:4

- detestable things (BDB 1054, cf. Lev. 11:10,11,12,13,20,23,41,42)

- mice (BDB 747, cf. Lev. 11:29)

I think the food laws of Leviticus 11 are not hygienic but cultic. They were meant to keep
Israel from any social or religious contact with Canaanites.

SPECIAL TOPIC: FOOD LAWS (OT)

verses.zh: 「我知道他们的行为和他们的意念。时候将到，我必将万民万族（族：原文是舌）聚来，看见我的荣耀，
verses.en: “I hate their deeds and thoughts! So I am coming[NOTE:1] to gather all the nations and ethnic groups;[NOTE:2] they will come and witness my splendor.
notes: The Hebrew text reads literally “and I, their deeds and their thoughts, am coming.” The syntax here is very problematic, suggesting that the text may need emendation. Some suggest that the words “their deeds and their thoughts” have been displaced from v. 17. This line presents two primary challenges. In the first place, the personal pronoun “I” has no verb after it. Most translations insert “know” for the sake of clarity (NASB, NRSV, NLT, ESV). The NIV11 has “I, because of what they have planned and done…” Since God’s “knowledge” of Israel’s sin occasions judgment, the verb “hate” is an option as well (see above translation). The feminine form of the next verb (בָּאָה, baʾah) could be understood in one of two ways. One could provide an implied noun “time” (עֵת, ʿet) and render the next line “the time is coming/has come” (NASB, ESV). One could also emend the feminine verb to the masculine בָּא (baʾ) and have the “I” at the beginning of the line govern this verb as well (for the Lord is speaking here): “I am coming” (cf. NIV, NCV, NRSV, TEV, NLT).
Heb “and the tongues”; KJV, NASB, NIV84, NRSV “and tongues”; NIV11 “and languages.”
verses.commentary:
66:18-21 "the time is coming to gather all nations and tongues" The word "time" has been
added by Eben Ezra in his translation of the Masoretic Text. There is some confusion as to the
exact setting of this verse. The VERB "know" is also not in the Hebrew text.

This is a reference somehow to the gathering of the nations. They seem to come for
hostile purposes against the people of God (i.e. "survivors"). But, in God's defeat of them (cf. Isa. 66:24b)
some come to believe in Him. Then God sends them as a sign, Isa. 66:19 (cf. Isa. 11:10,12), to their own
nations as evangelists. And, wonder of wonders - the heathen respond to the message and come back to
God at Jerusalem to worship and He even makes some of them into priests and Levites (cf. Isa. 61:6; 66:21).

This section, Isa. 66:19-24, is absolutely shocking in its universal thrust. This has
caused great consternation and uncertainty among the rabbis, but in context, it is obviously the fulfillment
of the Abrahamic promise of Gen. 3:15; 12:1-3.

SPECIAL TOPIC: YHWH'S ETERNAL REDEMPTIVE PLAN

66:18 "For I know their words and their thoughts" God knows the hearts of all humans. See full
note at Isa. 1:2. YHWH knows the thoughts and intentions of the heart (cf. 1 Sam. 2:3; 16:7; 1 Kgs. 8:39;
1 Chr. 28:9; 2 Chr. 6:30; Ps. 7:9; 17:3; 26:2; 44:21; 139:1,23; Prov. 15:11; 16:2; 21:2; 24:12; Isa. 66:18; Jer. 11:20;
17:9-10; 20:12; Luke 16:15; Acts 1:24; 15:8; Rom. 8:27). Jesus also knows the inner thoughts and motives
of humans, cf. John 2:24-25; 6:61,64; 13:11!

verses.zh: 我要显神迹（或译：记号）在他们中间。逃脱的，我要差到列国去，就是到他施、普勒、拉弓的路德和土巴、雅完，并素来没有听见我名声、没有看见我荣耀辽远的海岛；他们必将我的荣耀传扬在列国中。
verses.en: I will perform a mighty act among them[NOTE:1] and then send some of those who remain to the nations—to Tarshish, Pul,[NOTE:2] Lud[NOTE:3] (known for its archers[NOTE:4]), Tubal, Javan,[NOTE:5] and to the distant coastlands[NOTE:6] that have not heard about me or seen my splendor. They will tell the nations of my splendor.
notes: Heb “and I will set a sign among them.” The precise meaning of this statement is unclear. Elsewhere “to set a sign” means “perform a mighty act” (Ps 78:43; Jer 32:20), “make [someone] an object lesson” (Ezek 14:8), and “erect a [literal] standard” (Ps 74:4).
Some prefer to read “Put” (i.e., Libya).
That is, Lydia (in Asia Minor).
Heb “drawers of the bow” (KJV and ASV both similar).
Javan is generally identified today as Greece (so NIV, NCV, NLT).
Or “islands” (NIV).
verses.commentary:
66:19 "sign" See
SPECIAL TOPIC: SIGN

▣ "Tarshish" See SPECIAL TOPIC: TARSHISH.

▣ "Put" The MT has Pul (BDB 806, Peshitta, JPSOA, REB, NET), which refers to a place
in Babylon, but many modern translations (i.e. RSV, NEB) have "Put," which refers to Libya. The LXX has Phud,
which also refers to Libya.

▣ "Lud" The location of this ethnic group is uncertain.

- Gen. 10:13; 1 Chr. 1:11; Jer. 46:9 relate them to Egypt

- Gen. 10:22; 1 Chr. 1:17 relate them to Shem, making them Semites

- Ezek. 27:10 relates them to North Africa (related to Libya)

- Josephus, Antiquities of the Jews 1:144, relates them to Asia Minor (Jewish Study Bible, p. 916); related to Libya

▣ "Meshech, Rosh, Tubal" First "Meshech" is from the LXX. The MT has "those who draw the bow."
The UBS Text Project gives the LXX a "C" rating.

All of these names occur in Ezekiel 38 and refer to people groups in Asia Minor (i.e. Turkey).

▣ "Javan" This refers to Greece.

verses.en: They will bring back all your countrymen[NOTE:1] from all the nations as an offering to the Lord. They will bring them[NOTE:2] on horses, in chariots, in wagons, on mules, and on camels[NOTE:3] to my holy hill Jerusalem,” says the Lord, “just as the Israelites bring offerings to the Lord’s temple in ritually pure containers.
notes: Heb “brothers” (so NIV84); NIV11 “people”; NCV “fellow Israelites.”
The words “they will bring them” are supplied in the translation for stylistic reasons.
The precise meaning of this word is uncertain. Some suggest it refers to “chariots.” See HALOT 498 s.v. *כִּרְכָּרָה.
verses.commentary:
66:20 This is one of several texts that speak of the Gentile nations bringing gifts and offerings
(cf. Isa. 43:6; 49:22; 60:4; Micah 4:1-2) to Jerusalem/temple (cf. Isa. 2:2-3; 11:9; 56:7; 65:11,25; Ps. 22:27; 86:9; Jer. 3:17).
This verse refers to part of the offering of the nations will be the Israelite and Judean returnees!.

verses.en: “For just as the new heavens and the new earth I am about to make will remain standing before me,” says the Lord, “so your descendants and your name will remain.
verses.commentary:
66:22 For "the new heavens and the new earth," see full note at Isa. 65:17.

The VERB "endure" (BDB 763, KB 840) is used twice.

- the new heavens and earth will endure ‒ Qal IMPERFECT (see full note at
Isa. 62:2; also note Rev. 21-22)

- the seed of the faithful will endure ‒ Qal PERFECT with waw

This word, though used often in this section of Isaiah (cf. Isa. 44:11; 46:7; 47:12,13; 48:13; 50:8;
59:14; 61:5), is translated "endure" only in Isa. 66:22. It usually means "to stand."

verses.en: “They will go out and observe the corpses of those who rebelled against me, for the maggots that eat them will not die,[NOTE:1] and the fire that consumes them will not die out.[NOTE:2] All people will find the sight abhorrent.”[NOTE:3]
notes: Heb “for their worm will not die.”
Heb “and their fire will not be extinguished.”
Heb “and they will be an abhorrence to all flesh.”sn This verse depicts a huge mass burial site where the seemingly endless pile of maggot-infested corpses are being burned.
verses.commentary:
66:24 This is the description of the fate of the unfaithful of both covenant people and Gentiles. I do not think one can
build a theology of end-time punishment based on this verse. This is the possible source of Jesus' use of
the word Gehenna, which is a contraction of the phrase, "the valley of the sons of Hinnon," which was the place Judeans worshiped
Molech and was made into a garbage dump of Jerusalem. Jesus used this term to describe eternal separation
from God. Notice the elements of the worm that does not die and the fire that is not quenched. This is the imagery chosen
by Jesus Himself to describe the fate of those who refuse to believe in Him (cf. Matt. 25:46).

I personally am becoming more and more convinced of the theological opinion related to eternal
punishment called "limited immortality." Please see the following references.
